newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on technical correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on technical correction.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in dull trading on Thursday due to a technical correction after Wednesday's sharp falls, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,140 yuan ($2,306) per tonne, rising 150 yuan. It opened at 19,150 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 19,250 and a low of 19,120.
November rose 180 to 18,900, December 130 to 18,930, January 190 to 19,140, March 110 to 19,150, April 100 to 19,180 and May 120 to 19,200.
Combined volume fell to 40,450 tonnes from 117,570.
Copper opened higher and consolidated around its opening levels for most of the session.
Traders said short-covering pushed prices up, following heavy losses over the past few days.
"This was a normal technical correction and many speculators offset their short positions today because no further negative news emerged," one trader said.
"Large fluctuations in the past few days made many investors confused and they wanted to stay on the sidelines," he added.
Traders said the short-term market trend was not clear.
"Copper will find support at the 19,000-yuan level and strong support at 18,500 yuan, while it will meet resistance at 19,500 yuan," a second trader said.
Traders said LME would influence Shanghai's trend in the next few days in the absence of market-moving news.
Aluminium ended down. November did not trade. December fell 120 to 13,300 and January 100 to 13,300.
Combined volume rose to 220 tonnes from 160.
